summary: postinstall exfiltrates host identity and AWS execution metadata to Cloudflare tunnel
details: The package's postinstall.js executes automatically on npm install. It runs shell commands (`id`, `whoami`, `uname -a`, `hostname`, `cat /etc/passwd`), enumerates process.env to select AWS execution context variables (AWS_EXECUTION_ENV, AWS_LAMBDA_FUNCTION_NAME, AWS_ROLE_ARN, AWS_REGION, _HANDLER, LAMBDA_TASK_ROOT) plus CI markers, HOME/USER/PWD and npm user agent, and POSTs the JSON payload to https://encryption-watch-tubes-finger.trycloudflare.com/poc-b8f21a-exfil with a GET beacon fallback carrying whoami/hostname in the query string. The destination is an ephemeral Cloudflare Quick Tunnel, an anonymized throwaway hostname pattern used to evade domain-reputation controls. The exfiltrated data identifies the target AWS account/role and confirms execution inside CI or Lambda build environments — high-value reconnaissance for further AWS role abuse regardless of any self-labeling as a proof-of-concept.
